fault_protection_L3_002.notes: The task is a constructed coding scenario. No online source reproduces the exact prompt text (no contamination detected). The specific numerical parameters — Ia=1800 A, nominal load=100 A, threshold=5x=500 A, In values of 1750/30/1500 for the sample events — are hand-authored and do not appear in any retrieved source. The underlying engineering principles are well-established textbook knowledge: (1) threshold-based faulted phase detection using a multiple of load current (here 5x) to identify which phases are carrying fault current; (2) residual/zero-sequence current In=|Ia+Ib+Ic| distinguishing grounded faults (SLG, LLG: large In) from ungrounded faults (LL: near-zero In); (3) counting faulted phases to determine fault category. Retrieved sources confirm: the 11-class fault taxonomy (arxiv 2510.00831); zero-sequence = 0 for ideal LL faults and significant for LLG faults (industrialmonitordirect.com); standard four fault type definitions (turn2engineering.com). No source provides the specific threshold of 5x load or the exact numerical examples in the ground truth. Status is self_contained because the scenario and specific ground-truth numbers (current magnitudes, threshold, In values) are a constructed worked example, not extracted from a real measured dataset or published table. The underlying protection logic is standard and well-supported, making the ground truth technically sound, but the task itself is a hand-authored educational coding exercise.
